label: copy-phase input l (fed-back l), from the 2nd copy input onward
explanation: Fires when the token l is input during the copy phase, i.e. the model has just emitted l and it is fed back. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, including when l is first read as an original token. Activation is strong and fairly uniform (median ~4.1 of max 5.05) for copy steps with recall_idx >= 2. When l is the first fed-back input (recall_idx == 1, i.e. orig(0) == l) it fires only weakly and on a minority of those steps; that is the lowest-quartile tail. Magnitude does not vary with out_tok, prev_tok, or L. Almost no activation on any other input token (a few on j/p/t).

issues: No systematic counterexample found. Test: precision 1.0 (0 false positives), recall 0.978, F1 0.989, mass recall 0.999.

All 1675 test misses are copy-phase l inputs at recall_idx == 1 (sequences starting with l), with relative activation 0.01-0.09. This matches the explanation's weak tail. Dev: 1636 active of about 12.5k such steps, roughly 13%.
Phase claims hold: 0 activations in the original and delimiter phases, including original-phase l.
Off-token activity is negligible: j 17, p 3, t 1 steps on dev, out of 76170 active.
Minor: the label 'from the 2nd copy input onward' leaves out the weak, sparse firing at recall_idx 1. The explanation states it, so this is not an overclaim.
